system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation (and one-line reason) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped in aggregate at **AUD 4.8m (20% of price)**. | A materially higher general-warranty cap, ideally **100% of price**, or at least a level supported by diligence and risk; separate, higher caps for specific risks. | **Reject 20%; seek a substantially higher cap.** A 20% ceiling may not cover material losses across the warranty package. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 tipping basket, with only the excess recoverable. | A lower de minimis and a lower tipping basket—or a deductible basket where recovery begins only above the threshold—plus exclusions for specific and fundamental claims. | **Seek lower thresholds and a tipping basket.** The proposed thresholds screen out smaller claims and leave the Buyer bearing the first AUD 250,000. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General claims must be notified within **18 months**; Seller says any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | A longer period (commonly negotiated by reference to the business and diligence); clear survival periods for each claim category, with tax claims tied to the relevant statutory period and no blanket extension of general limits to other claims. | **Reject the blanket rule and negotiate category-specific periods.** Different claims need different survival periods, and an 18-month window may be too short to discover latent issues. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties. | Separate fundamental/title regime with a substantially higher cap (ideally price-level), longer survival, and appropriate threshold carve-outs. | **Reject parity with general warranties.** The Buyer is paying for the shares and should have stronger recourse if ownership or authority is defective. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no express fraud carve-out is stated. | Expressly exclude fraud (including fraudulent misrepresentation and fraud by or on behalf of the Seller, as legally appropriate) from caps, thresholds, time bars, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance protections. | **Require an express fraud carve-out.** The Seller should not be able to contractually cap or exclude liability for its own fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire indexed data room as at 22 September 2026, plus accounts, statutory registers and public records; specific disclosures add detail. | Specific, fair, sufficiently detailed disclosures against the relevant warranties; no blanket data-room or public-record disclosure, and a clear index/cut-off and access record. | **Reject general disclosure as drafted.** Blanket disclosure makes it difficult to assess which facts qualify which warranties and whether disclosure was adequate. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | No broad imputed or constructive knowledge bar; if any knowledge qualifier is accepted, limit it to actual knowledge of named individuals after reasonable inquiry and expressly preserve claims for disclosed matters unless specifically agreed. | **Reject the clause as drafted.** “Discoverable” knowledge is broad and could turn diligence access into a waiver of warranty protection. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller will use reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty’s written consent. DD-002 indicates about AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%) and consent conditions; final consent and evidence conditions are absent. | A condition precedent to Completion requiring valid written consent and satisfaction/waiver of all conditions; alternatively, a Buyer termination right or agreed protection if not obtained by long-stop. | **Make effective consent and condition satisfaction a completion condition.** Bluefen is a major revenue source and consent alone may not satisfy clause 11.3. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to follow Completion. DD-003 says facility remains unpaid and no final security discharge is included. | Repayment and discharge of the facility and security at or before Completion, evidenced by lender documents and reflected in completion funds flow; no post-Completion release risk to Buyer. | **Require simultaneous payoff and discharge at Completion.** A promise of release afterwards leaves the acquired company exposed to debt and security risk. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 conditional Completion bonuses are treated as Seller’s matter and omitted from funds flow; on-costs are unspecified. | Determine the amount and treatment of bonuses and all payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs; have Seller fund them or deduct them as debt-like/leakage amounts under agreed price mechanics, with payment and liability allocation documented. | **Do not leave them outside the funds flow.** The Buyer should not unknowingly fund Seller-period compensation or associated liabilities. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; Seller considers it adequate. DD-004 says materials transfer only after all SOW3 fees are cleared; DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, without independent payment verification or confirmatory assignment. | A specific indemnity covering payment, ownership/assignment, access and use of all relevant Project Materials, third-party claims and remediation; preferably require cleared payment and executed assignment before Completion. | **Expand the indemnity and secure the IP transfer at Completion.** The disclosed records do not establish payment or that the Company owns the materials it needs. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Seller characterises DD-006 as preliminary and not expected to be material; no specific protection is offered in the update. Disclosure says access, scope and notification position remain unknown. | Completion deliverables on investigation and containment, required notices/cooperation, a specific indemnity for incident-related losses and costs, and tailored warranty/claim treatment; preserve post-Completion access to evidence and cooperation. | **Treat as an unresolved specific risk, not merely an ordinary warranty matter.** The potential personal-information exposure is unquantified and its notification implications remain unknown. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals total AUD 330,000, described as ordinary-course operating costs. DD-008/011 do not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. | Reconcile renewal terms, timing, termination rights, accruals and whether liabilities are reflected in accounts or price mechanics; seek a specific adjustment or protection for any undisclosed or non-ordinary commitment. | **Do not accept the “ordinary course” label without verification.** The combined records leave the nature and financial treatment of the AUD 330,000 commitment unclear. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; Seller says limits apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise and treats tax/IP under the general regime. | Expressly distinguish general warranty, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnity, covenant, debt/price adjustment and fraud claims, with tailored caps, thresholds, time limits and remedies. | **Add an express category-by-category regime.** Otherwise general limitations may unintentionally restrict claims that should have separate treatment. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register recording it as holder of 100%; no independent Buyer verification is described. | Verify the register against ASIC/company records and constitutional/corporate documents, confirm all issued shares and absence of options, liens or other interests, and obtain duly executed transfers and releases at Completion. | **Do not treat the register alone as conclusive.** Verify title and deliver clean transfer mechanics and appropriate title warranties at Completion. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime, including the general cap and time limits. | Negotiate express tax and IP warranties and, where justified, specific indemnities; set separate caps and survival periods (tax aligned to relevant assessment periods) and confirm the Ironquay transfer is covered. | **Keep tax and IP open pending express drafting.** The Seller’s assertion does not resolve the substantive protection or the known Ironquay ownership/payment issue. |

This is a buyer-side issue list based on the supplied update and disclosure letter; final positions should be checked against the complete SPA, schedules, funds flow and underlying diligence records.
=== END ADVICE ===
